title: Moai of Rapa Nui (Easter Island)
summary: The moai are about 887 monolithic human figures carved by the Polynesian society of Rapa Nui (Easter Island), Chile, between roughly the 10th and 16th centuries, most of them at the Rano Raraku quarry. The average statue is about 4 m tall. The island park has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1995.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO says the shrines and moai were built from the 10th to the 16th century; the exact start is not given.

reviewer_note: Shape: statue_group. The pin is the Rano Raraku quarry, where 397 statues remain; the 887 are spread over the island on scattered platforms. Typical height 13 ft (about 4 m) is NOVA's average; UNESCO gives a 2-20 m range. The plan dimension is the island length (14 miles, Smithsonian Magazine). The date range is UNESCO's; other sources date carving to 1250-1500.
